---
title: "check-exercise-question-paragraph.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that fails a pull request which adds a paragraph of an exercise
that mixes scenario information with the instruction or question.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-11-02) is that the task of an exercise
goes in its own paragraph, apart from the scenario information.

The check looks at each exercise div (`#exr-...`).
A sentence is a task when it ends with a question mark
or starts with an imperative task verb
such as Show, Find, Compute, Estimate, Explain or Derive.
Every other sentence of prose counts as scenario.
A paragraph with both kinds is reported.
Sentences are found by punctuation,
so a sentence broken across lines at a clause counts once.

Solutions, callouts such as hints, code fences, display math, lists, tables,
headings and HTML comments are not examined.
`<!-- question-paragraph-ok: reason -->` inside an exercise exempts it.

An untouched paragraph is never reflagged.
With no base ref the check skips instead of scanning the whole tree;
`whole-tree` measures a corpus.

## Usage

Copy
[`examples/check-exercise-question-paragraph.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-exercise-question-paragraph.yml)
to `.github/workflows/` in your repository.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | `*.qmd` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check |
| `fail` | `true` | Fail the workflow on a finding; `false` gives warnings only |
| `whole-tree` | `false` | Scan every exercise, not only a PR's additions |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version to set up |
